newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina decries shipping of nuclear waste.
newsitem.headline: Argentina decries shipping of nuclear waste.

text.p: Argentina on Wednesday urged Japan, France and Britain to stop ferrying nuclear waste around the world and said it would take unspecified steps if ships bearing such cargo passed near its coast.

"Bearing in mind the excellent ties we have with the governments of Japan, France and Britain, we urge them not to repeat this kind of shipment in the future," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Argentina, Chile and Brazil all complained when the radioactive material passed close to their shores last March.
Buenos Aires warned on Wednesday it would take "steps recognised by the international law to preserve the maritime ecosystem and the health of its inhabitants."
It did not specify what measures it would take and no one was immediately available for comment at the Foreign Ministry.
The statement came two days after a British-registered ship left the French harbour of Cherbourg with waste from fuel that was recycled in France for Japan.

But unlike the incident last March, when the ship passed by Argentina's southernmost tip, the freighter was reported to be taking a different route, from France to the southern tip of South Africa and east to Japan.
The 5,000-ton ship carrying 20 metric tons of nuclear waste was expected to arrive in Japan in March. A total of 30 shipments of this kind have been scheduled.
